hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach police arrest Boca Raton man for soliciting videos from 14-year-old
cards.teaser: Maximiliano Buitrago, 51, of Boca Raton was arrested after responding to an undercover Craigslist post offering babysitting services and asking a supposed 14-year-old for videos in exchange for money.
cards.body:
A Boca Raton man faces charges of solicitation to commit human trafficking and unlawful use of a two-way communication device after allegedly attempting to solicit videos from someone he believed to be a 14-year-old girl, according to Boynton Beach police. Maximiliano Buitrago, 51, was arrested following an undercover operation conducted by the department's Human Exploitation Unit.

Investigators say Buitrago responded to a Craigslist advertisement offering summer babysitting services that had been posted by undercover detectives. According to police, he contacted the supposed minor and asked, "Are you trying to make cash any other way? What else can you do?" During their communications, Buitrago repeatedly acknowledged that the girl was 14 years old, investigators say. He allegedly offered her money for videos, claiming they would be viewed by clients overseas.

On July 16, Buitrago arranged to meet with the girl at a park in Boynton Beach. When he arrived at the location, police took him into custody. Officers searched his vehicle and found cards that read, "Make money on TikTok with pics and short videos," which also included an offer to "get paid cash." Following his arrest, Buitrago confessed to investigators, according to police. He is currently being held at the Palm Beach County jail.

Boynton Beach police believe there may be additional victims and are asking the public for help in the investigation. Anyone who may have received one of the cards found in Buitrago's vehicle or who communicated with him is encouraged to contact BBPD Detective Joseph at 561-742-6158. The arrest highlights ongoing efforts by law enforcement to combat human trafficking and the exploitation of minors through undercover operations targeting predators who use online platforms to identify potential victims.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast residents avoid lettuce after E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks
cards.teaser: As reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid.
cards.body:
Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, and many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid. The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are just trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Jenny Rhodes said the changes have meant giving up some favorite foods, saying she misses her salads and berries. George Lorenz said he is trying to stay away from it while grabbing lunch with his father Brian on Clematis Street in downtown West Palm Beach. Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like bananas, melons and avocados, and should wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them. Barone said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. She recommends avoiding bagged lettuce if possible and instead buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers.

cards.headline: Florida state Rep. Fabian Basabe ordered to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment, battery case
cards.body:
A Leon County jury ordered Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 after finding him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The civil judgment came at the end of a trial brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself in court despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders.

Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told Basabe directly that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned. Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. However, after the verdict, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. The judge's comments underscored the severity of Basabe's courtroom conduct during the proceedings.

Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations against him. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. Despite the civil judgment, Basabe maintains his innocence regarding the claims of sexual harassment, battery and defamation brought by the plaintiffs. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation following the verdict.

Basabe is seeking reelection this fall. The verdict could renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action against him. The case represents a significant legal setback for the Republican lawmaker as he campaigns to retain his seat. The $450,000 judgment reflects the jury's findings on multiple claims including sexual harassment, battery and defamation brought by two former staff members and the mother of one of them.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates and that carriers adjust their service based on passenger demand. JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route received enough time to establish itself. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized that the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is difficult to match. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Meanwhile, the airline's Boston route from Vero Beach continues to perform well, with Dambeck noting that Boston is seeing great demand. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. The cancellation represents a setback for local travelers who had welcomed the direct connection to New York when it launched less than a year ago, though the continued success of the Boston route demonstrates ongoing viability for JetBlue service at the regional airport.

cards.headline: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon faces September trial on charges from Capitol sit-in
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave.

Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. She is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary. The trial is scheduled after the primary. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman. Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter and has pushed his total receipts above $16 million for the Senate race.

cards.headline: South Florida residents avoid lettuce, berries amid E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks
cards.teaser: Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, and many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid.
cards.body:
The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. Jenny Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with her children Dakota and Brynlee, said she misses salads and berries but would rather be careful than ruin her day. George Lorenz said he is taking precautions while grabbing lunch with his father, Brian, on Clematis Street in downtown West Palm Beach. Hendriette Peckens said in Boynton Beach that she bought two big bags of oranges, bread and some apples, avoiding produce because of the outbreak while planning to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner. Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

hero.headline: Five cyclospora cases confirmed across Treasure Coast counties since May
hero.teaser: Health officials report cyclospora infections in St. Lucie, Martin and Palm Beach counties as contaminated lettuce outbreaks spread nationwide.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The cases come as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, with many South Florida residents changing what they eat and what they avoid.

The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. The outbreaks can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Some families are steering clear of leafy greens altogether, with Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes visiting Delray Beach saying they are trying to stay away from lettuce. Their mother Jenny Rhodes said she misses her salads and berries but believes it is better to be careful. In downtown West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he has heard about the outbreak and is trying to stay away from contaminated produce. Shoppers in Boynton Beach have been loading carts with alternatives, with Hendriette Peckens saying she bought oranges, bread and apples and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She also said the trick is to still wash them before cutting into them and peeling them, which includes foods like bananas, melons and avocados. Barone recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. She emphasized that the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating entirely.

Barone's biggest warning is to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. Instead, she recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a one to three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce. She also suggests making sure to cook vegetables when possible.

cards.headline: Florida voter registration data downloaded by Chinese cyber actor in 2022, declassified records show
cards.teaser: Newly released intelligence records show Florida was among six states whose publicly available voter information was downloaded from commercial websites.
cards.body:
Declassified records released by the White House show a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public opinion analysis.

The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots. The disclosure came during Trump's Thursday address to Congress, in which he urged lawmakers to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeated claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated.

cards.headline: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon gets September trial date for Capitol sit-in charges
cards.teaser: The Jacksonville legislator will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges from her May protest outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. She said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman.

Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach firefighters rescue dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes after it fell 10 to 12 feet into raw sewage.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosts resource fair in Loxahatchee for veterans
cards.teaser: VA representatives assisted veterans with eligibility, enrollment and claims support at Big Dog Ranch Rescue on Friday.
cards.body:
The West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosted a resource fair for veterans on Friday at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee. VA representatives assisted veterans with eligibility and health care enrollment, VA health care programs and claims support. A mobile medical unit was on site to address basic medical needs and allowed veterans to complete an initial primary care appointment on site and get into the VA system on the spot. Richard "Buzz" Bryan, director of community relations and community engagement for the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System, said the event focused on reaching veterans who have not yet connected with VA services. Bryan, a combat veteran himself, said he did not utilize VA services for years and wants other veterans to learn from his experience.

Big Dog Ranch Rescue was on site to provide information about its service dog training program, animal adoption opportunities and additional veteran-focused services. Bryan said the organization's veteran service program is outstanding and called it the best place to get a service animal. Veterans who were unable to attend the resource fair can call the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System at (561) 422-8387 to access enrollment and health care resources.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new administration area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district said barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. In the meantime, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said these animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very, very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

hero.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making game decisions
hero.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday night to prevent teams from using AI for substitutions and pitch calling.
hero.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that the custom tab had expanded the use of dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting the prohibition at the start of the second half was intended to provide clubs that had relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Argentina beats England 2-1 in World Cup semifinal with late goals from Fernandez and Martinez
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday and advance to the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina scored twice in the final moments for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday. Enzo Fernandez swept in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time off a cross from Lionel Messi.

England captain Harry Kane scored the opening goal in the 55th minute through Anthony Gordon. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks. Alexis Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina pressed for an equalizer.

The defending champions will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina has now eliminated England from the World Cup in 1986, 1998, and 2026. England coach Thomas Tuchel said his substitutions seemed more intent on holding the lead rather than scoring a second goal.

cards.headline: Photographer who captured Messi bathing infant Yamal reflects on images ahead of World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photos taken in 2007 of Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal have gone viral before Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press from his home in Barcelona, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed now with the World Cup final looming between Messi's Argentina and Yamal's Spain. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets. The 58-year-old photographer said he will have trouble cheering for one team or the other in Sunday's final, when the 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior. He has an everlasting love for Messi, the best player of all time, but Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain, thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

cards.headline: FBI seizes hundreds of drones near stadiums during World Cup as final security tightens
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies have spent two years preparing security for Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey.
cards.body:
The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be addressed from a threat perspective. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Spain faces Argentina in World Cup final Sunday as Yamal, 19, meets Messi, 39
cards.teaser: The 2026 FIFA World Cup comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey between Argentina and Spain.
cards.body:
Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute after Anthony Gordon scored for England in the 55th minute, Argentina fought back when Fernandez swept in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Alexis Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Messi, now 39 and likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from further strengthening his case to be considered the greatest soccer player of all time. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team is going to try to win and leave everything out there. He said it is very difficult to get people to understand what these players are showing, calling the team unique. Argentina is now one step away from back-to-back World Cup titles.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts from Treasure Coast finish top 15 at nationals, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer qualified for the Junior Olympics after securing a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a team throughout what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season that included local competitions, travel meets, states, and regionals. The trio came close to a perfect score at nationals, earning a 9.9. Lazuka said it's hard to get a perfect 10, making the team's 9.9 particularly notable.

Each gymnast came to the sport for different reasons. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics that drew her in, but rather the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they looked and how fun the sport appeared. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. The team will compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about qualifying as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Edge Palm Beach 3-2 in Extra Innings
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored the deciding run in the top of the 10th before Miguel Mejias retired the Cardinals in order to close it out, giving the Mets a 1-0 lead in the three-game series.

Palm Beach struck first on a Sebastian Dos Santos solo home run in the bottom of the first. The early deficit was a tall order for St. Lucie, which came in 16-34 on the season when allowing the first run.

Randy Guzman answered in a hurry in his first game back from the injured list, where he had been since June 9. In his first at-bat, Guzman launched a 108 mph solo homer 374 feet to left to tie it at 1-1 in the second. It was his 10th home run of the season.

Palm Beach edged back ahead in the bottom of the second on a fielder's choice, but St. Lucie answered again when Elian Pena hit his fourth home run of the year to level the score at 2-2.

From there it became a pitchers' duel. Mets starter Joel Lara allowed two runs on four hits over 4 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out five. Zack Mack followed with 1 1/3 scoreless innings and two strikeouts, and Elwis Mijares handled the next three innings, allowing just two hits with no walks and three strikeouts. Mijares earned the win to improve to 4-4.

With the score still tied in the 10th, the Mets started the inning with automatic runner AJ Salgado at second. Branny De Oleo moved him to third with a sacrifice bunt, and Chase Meggers brought him home on a sacrifice fly for a 3-2 lead.

Mejias took the bottom of the 10th and delivered a perfect frame, striking out two before getting Matthew Miura to pop out to end it, earning his second save of the season.

The Mets improved to 7-13 in the second half and 40-46 overall. Palm Beach fell to 12-9 in the second half and 45-42 overall. St. Lucie can lock up the series Saturday night, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m. at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

hero.headline: Florida state Rep. Fabian Basabe ordered to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment, battery case
hero.body:
A Leon County jury ordered Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 after finding him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The civil judgment came at the end of a trial brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself in court despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders.

Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told Basabe directly that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned. Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. However, after the verdict, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. The judge's comments underscored the severity of Basabe's courtroom conduct during the proceedings.

Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations against him. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. Despite the civil judgment, Basabe maintains his innocence regarding the claims of sexual harassment, battery and defamation brought by the plaintiffs. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation following the verdict.

Basabe is seeking reelection this fall. The verdict could renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action against him. The case represents a significant legal setback for the Republican lawmaker as he campaigns to retain his seat. The $450,000 judgment reflects the jury's findings on multiple claims including sexual harassment, battery and defamation brought by two former staff members and the mother of one of them.

cards.headline: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon faces September trial on charges from Capitol sit-in
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave.

Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. She is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary. The trial is scheduled after the primary. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman. Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter and has pushed his total receipts above $16 million for the Senate race.

cards.headline: Alex Vindman raises $8.5 million in Florida Senate race, expands fundraising lead over Nixon
cards.teaser: Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million.
cards.body:
Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Vindman said he thinks it is safe to say that Republicans woke up this morning with a bit of a panic, adding there is no denying that the Florida Senate race is in play. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup.

Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term. Vindman is challenging Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon for the Democratic Senate nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary. Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave following several hours of protest against Florida's newly approved congressional map.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels' low Pensacola beach flyover despite safety concerns
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is sticking to encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels jet buzzed a Pensacola beach so low that chairs and tents went flying and sand kicked up.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's Blue Angels demonstration squadron flying so low over a crowded Pensacola beach on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, a host of Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote carry on patriots on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet with the words freedom and it's okay to love America.

It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration political appointee, said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior.

cards.headline: South Florida residents avoid lettuce, berries amid E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks
cards.teaser: Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, and many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid.
cards.body:
The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. Jenny Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with her children Dakota and Brynlee, said she misses salads and berries but would rather be careful than ruin her day. George Lorenz said he is taking precautions while grabbing lunch with his father, Brian, on Clematis Street in downtown West Palm Beach. Hendriette Peckens said in Boynton Beach that she bought two big bags of oranges, bread and some apples, avoiding produce because of the outbreak while planning to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner. Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

cards.headline: Declassified records show Chinese cyber actor downloaded Florida voter registration data in 2022
cards.teaser: Declassified records released by the White House say a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022.
cards.body:
One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown.

The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots. The disclosure came during President Donald Trump's Thursday national address, during which he urged Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeated claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump said during his address that mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt, though he did not single out Florida.

cards.headline: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces eligibility challenge in Florida court
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary in court next week.
cards.body:
Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida.

The court fight represents another political legal battle in Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary. The case could determine whether Fishback remains on the ballot for the August primary.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million from $20 scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the Florida Lottery's $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The ticket cost $20.

The overall odds of winning the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH game are 1-in-2.90. The odds of winning the $5 million top prize are 1-in-4,018,135.

Florida Lottery officials released the information Friday in a public statement about recent winners across the state.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He noted that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. However, he said the Boston route from Vero Beach Regional Airport is performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He praised the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

Dambeck said JetBlue will continue to evaluate the JFK route, so it could return in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.
